name: Skipping Stone
description: Echoes that land like a stone skipping over water: closer and closer together, each softer and duller, crossing from one side to the other. Or the other way, slowing down and spreading out. Both sides are summed into the skips.

params.name: First
params.description: How long after the sound the first skip lands. Every later gap is measured from this one, so it sets the pace of the whole throw.

params.name: Bounce
params.description: The length of each gap against the one before. Below the middle the skips close up and hurry, above it they slow down and spread out.

params.name: Skips
params.description: How many times the stone lands. The skips share the level of the sound between them, so more skips are each softer. The throw ends early once the gaps get too short.

params.name: Loss
params.description: How much softer each skip is than the one before. At zero every landing is as loud as the first. The whole throw stays as loud, so more Loss brings the first skips up.

params.name: Sink
params.description: How much duller each skip is than the one before. Turned up, the late landings are only a low thud.

params.name: Drop
params.description: Lowers each skip in pitch a little more than the one before, up to a whole tone a skip. Held notes beat between the skips. A sharp attack can land a touch early or late.

params.name: Throw
params.description: Carries the skips across the stereo field as they go, left to right or the other way, and in the middle they stay put. The skips are made of both sides summed.

params.name: Ripple
params.description: Blurs the skips into rings, a little more with each one. The first landing stays sharp and the last ones spread into a wash.

params.name: Again
params.description: Throws the stone again from where it stopped, at this share of the throw before. Turned up, whole throws keep coming, each duller and lower. A held sound cannot pile up.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the skips.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A multi-tap delay whose tap times follow a geometric series, with per-tap loss, low-pass, pan and delay-line pitch drop, a shared allpass diffuser fed more by each later tap, and feedback from the last tap. Not a model of any unit.
